title: Space and the planets for kids
examples: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
How far away is the Moon from Earth?
Are all the planets the same size?

explain.say: The Sun is a giant star. It gives us light and heat.

draw.text: Space and the planets for kids

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: the solar system. Can you see the sun and the mercury? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Space and the planets for kids

explain.say: Our solar system has eight planets that go around the Sun. They are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
The Moon orbits the Earth. It does not make its own light. It only reflects the Sun's light.
Stars are giant, burning balls of gas, just like the Sun. They are very far away from us.

items: Stars are giant balls of gas

explain.say: Imagine you are watching the Moon at night. The Moon always follows a path around the Earth.
When we look up at the night sky, we see many stars. They twinkle because of Earth's air.

faq.q: Why is the Sun so important to us?
faq.a: The Sun provides the light that lets us see during the day. It also gives us the heat that keeps Earth warm enough for life.
asks: What does the Sun give off?
Is the Sun like a giant lamp?

faq.q: Does the Moon make any light?
faq.a: No, the Moon does not make its own light. It only shines because it bounces the light from the Sun back to our eyes.
asks: Where does the Moon get its light?
Can the Moon shine at night?

faq.q: Are all the planets the same size?
faq.a: No, the planets are very different sizes. Jupiter is much bigger than Earth, for example.
asks: Are all planets the same size?

faq.q: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
faq.a: A star, like the Sun, makes its own light and heat through burning. A planet, like Earth, goes around a star.
asks: What is the main difference between stars and planets?

faq.a: The solar system is our neighborhood in space. It includes the Sun, the planets, and other things that orbit it.
asks: What is everything in space called?
What makes up our solar system?

facts: The Sun is a star, not a planet.
The eight planets orbit the Sun in order.
Stars shine because they produce their own energy.

quiz.say: Which object is a star and produces its own light?
quiz.why: The Sun is a star, and all stars create their own light and heat.

wrong.0: Planets orbit stars; they do not create their own light.
wrong.1: The Moon only reflects light from other sources.
wrong.2: Earth is a planet, not a star.

quiz.say: What is the main body that the Moon orbits?
quiz.why: The Moon is known to travel in an orbit around the Earth.

wrong.1: The Sun is too far away for the Moon to orbit it directly.
wrong.2: Mars is a planet, not the main body the Moon orbits.
wrong.3: The Moon does not orbit itself.

quiz.say: If you see something shining brightly at night, is it more likely to be a star or a planet?
quiz.why: Stars are distant, burning balls of gas that shine very brightly.

wrong.0: The Moon's light is only reflected light, not its own shine.
wrong.1: Comets are different objects that change appearance.
wrong.3: Planets are much closer and usually appear dimmer than stars.
